ci_at_b4ec8b7.diagnosis: The unchanged test globally patches time.time with three values. A local probe reproduced exhaustion when another clock caller consumed a value; a module-isolated clock preserved the three throttling assertions. The six focused throttle tests passed unchanged in isolation.
ci_at_b4ec8b7.fix: Patch the composition module time binding, leaving other clock users independent; retain the first/blocked/delayed handler assertions and assert that an independent clock read does not consume the throttle sequence.

environment_notes: Each downstream test used a temporary git-archive source snapshot and isolated venv with the CI wheel installed locally. Existing dependency libraries were borrowed through a .pth file; the Praval Code native harness package was copied into the temporary snapshot. Active installations were unchanged.

PravalClaw used Python 3.14 with freshly resolved candidate framework dependencies and temporary Path.home defaults. Praval Code used Python 3.12; standalone provider and wheel schema checks used Python 3.13.
No deployment, server context setting, model variant creation or real connector delivery was performed.

initial_attempts.details: The first launcher used --trust alone, leaving shell approval pending in noninteractive mode. Both models executed file tools but pytest was rejected. The initial verifier also looked for legacy praval_turns.jsonl instead of the current effect history. Corrected runs used --auto-approve within the temporary workspace and asserted the current effect records; both passed.

Used a temporary UV_CACHE_DIR after sandbox access to the default cache was denied; copied the existing native harness dependency for Praval Code; installed candidate framework dependencies in the temporary PravalClaw environment; reran the Code pytest suite with process permissions required by its plugin.

limits: Gemini Flash-Lite passed again using the new key. Gemini 3.5 Flash made one valid tool call before HTTP 429 free-tier quota exhaustion blocked continuation; that model has no complete live certificate.
PravalClaw suite uses isolated deterministic providers and fake connectors; live deployment and outbound delivery are unverified.
Praval Code token accounting was complete; no model prices were configured, so estimated cost was unavailable and costComplete was false.
